Price shape. Mostly one-time or free. Obsidian's core is free with paid sync at around $50 a year, which is the main ongoing cost in this category.

## The thing almost none of them do

None of these apps renders Markdown in Finder.

You still cannot select a `.md` file, press space, and read it. Every one of them requires opening the app first, which is a lot of ceremony for glancing at a README.

Fixing that needs a Quick Look extension. QLMarkdown does it free and open source. TypeFire bundles one with an editor, which is the only combination of the two in this list.

It sounds minor. In practice, reading is most of what people do with Markdown files, and it is the interaction every editor ignores.

# Best Markdown Editor for Mac in 2026: 8 Apps Compared

August 11, 2026by TypeFire

best markdown editor macmarkdown editor macfree markdown editor mactypora vs obsidianmarkdown app mac

There is no single best Markdown editor, because "Markdown editor" covers at least three different jobs: writing long form, managing a library of linked notes, and reading files other people wrote.

Here are eight apps, what each is genuinely best at, and the feature almost none of them have.

Best Markdown Editor for Mac in 2026: 8 Apps Compared

## Quick picks [...] Prices checked August 2026.

## What separates them

Editing model. Typora hides syntax as you type, so you see formatted text and never raw Markdown. MacDown shows source and rendered side by side. VS Code shows source with an optional preview pane. None is objectively right: WYSIWYG is calmer for prose, split panes are better when the exact syntax matters.

Whether it manages files. Typora and MacDown open a document. Obsidian manages a vault, with backlinks, tags and a graph. That is a much bigger commitment and much more powerful if you want it.

Export. If you publish out of your editor, Typora and Marked 2 are far ahead: PDF, Word, HTML, LaTeX, with themes.
